# Kyverno CRD Enhancements

## Explanation

This pull request introduces enhancements for managing Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) in Kyverno. These changes aim to improve how CRDs are validated and governed, making it easier for users to enforce policies across their Kubernetes environments. This PR represents a feature addition to enhance existing capabilities.

## Related Issue

[Closes #1234. Discussed with @JimBugwadia.
](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/10635#issue-2398848176)
## Milestone of this PR

/milestone 1.2.3

## Documentation (required for features)

My PR contains new or altered behavior in Kyverno. 
- [ ] I have sent the draft PR to add or update [the documentation](https://github.com/kyverno/website) and the link is:
  <!-- https://github.com/kyverno/website/pull/123 -->

## What Type of PR is This

/kind feature

## Proposed Changes

This PR implements new functionality for CRD management in Kyverno, including validation rules and error handling improvements. These enhancements will enable users to maintain better control over their custom resources, ensuring compliance with organizational policies.

### Proof Manifests

## Example Commands

To create permissions for Vertical Pod Autoscalers, run the following command:

```bash
./kubectl-kyverno create cluster-role vpa --resources=verticalpodautoscalers --api-groups=autoscaling.k8s.io --verbs=all --controllers=kyverno-background-controller --controllers=kyverno-admission-controller
```

**Command Output:**
```bash
clusterrole.rbac.authorization.k8s.io/kyverno-verticalpodautoscalers-permission unchanged
```

To apply the VPA recommender policy, use:

```bash
kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JimBugwadia/kyverno-policies-VPA/main/generate-vpa-recommender/generate-vpa-recommender.yaml
```

**Command Output:**
```bash
clusterpolicy.kyverno.io/generate-vpa-recommender configured
```

## Which issue does this PR close?

While working with `MemoryExec`, I noticed it's output is pretty ugly, especially with `dbg!` where I'd expect output across multiple lines.

I don't necessarily agree with the subset of fields included, but I didn't change it.

## Rationale for this change

Make `MemoryExec` easy to understand.

## What changes are included in this PR?

Change the impl of `fmt::Debug` for `MemoryExec` to use the standard `debug_struct` approach

## Are these changes tested?

No, `Debug` implementations generally aren't. I ran it locally.

## Are there any user-facing changes?

no

body: Description ----------- Enables https://github.com/buzhidaotw/bzd-internal/issues/10 by adding support for voting weight per season token. * Currently this is hardcoded to weight 1 for season 2 (token ID: 2) and weight 0.5 for season 1 (token ID: 1) * Having voting power > 0, so either token, gives you the ability to participate. * Quorum is calculated as 20% on the sum of `# of members per season * season voting weight` for all seasons. Mumbai support has been removed since Polygon mumbai testnet is no longer around so removed mumbai support until we support membership nft contract on a different testnet. - [x] Change MSRV back to 1.74
- [x] Uncomment `unwrap_used` lint
- [x] Remove #[inline] attributes
- [x] Keep the option to use the single-writer transaction type

author: wardenpotato
body:
Its finally here, the rework of the outline library which started because of https://github.com/TTT-2/TTT2/issues/1411
Ive spent quite some time on this trying over 50 different approaches, running into various setbacks each time.
Some of them got solved: https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod-issues/issues/5744
And some didnt: https://github.com/Facepunch/garrysmod-requests/issues/2308

But this is what i consider the best thats possible in gmod today in respect to functionality and performance.

This rework includes(i may have forgotten some, its been a while):
- A switch to using the zbuffer instead of line of sight checking every single entity
- Outline thickness option
- Multiple render types for outlines
- More performant drawing
- Drawing not breaking when scopes are used in weapon addons
- Full documentation
- Fixed outlines being thinner on one side than the other

The comments in the code explain a lot so i hope those answer most questions.

author: zhanwenchen
body:
Currently,  all Exceptions are caught and few, if any, are reraised. This prohibits any fatal exceptions from forcing a system exit. Essentially, we want to catch and reraise fatal errors (`SystemExit`s) independently from generic `Exception`s  like this:

From:
```python
try:
    ...
except Exception as e:
    print(...)
    pass
```

To:
```python
try:
    ...
except SystemExit as e:
    raise SystemExit('FATAL ERROR ...') from e
except Exception as e:
    print(...)
    pass
```

See equivalent issue in my fork: https://github.com/zhanwenchen/AgentBoard/issues/1

body:
This rewrite cleans up a lot of unused packages along with updating many of the existing libraries. This was mainly to see if we could get the status bar to change colors in iOS, and we discovered that the PWA and/or its manifest is the limiting factor.

If you comment out the PWA manifest, then the status bar will switch with the dark/light mode switch in Safari. However, the PWA is more valuable to keep. So this ends up cleaning things up while establishing that baseline knowledge for future research.

author: umbraloptimatum
body: Talking to various NPCs that mention rare pokemon now reveal their silhouettes in the pokedex. Closes approved suggestion #3578. ## Description `RoamerNPC`s already reveal the mentioned pokemon in the pokedex, now regular NPCs can as well. I added flags to a whole bunch of quest NPCs plus the couple NPCs that directly mention legendary/mythical pokemon. As part of this, I fixed some issues with how the pokedex handles seen-but-uncaught pokemon: - `Statistics.pokemonSeen` was confusingly named: it's only used for pokemon that haven't been encountered, a completely different meaning than `PokedexHelper.pokemonSeen()`. It's now `Statistics.pokemonDiscovered`. - The pokedex now differentiates properly between discovered and seen pokemon, only showing silhouettes for the former. This means pokemon revealed by `RoamerNPC`s will no longer display their name or let you access the statistics modal. - If we want to, we could make discovered pokemon display their name to distinguish them from completely-undiscovered species that just have lower ID than a known species. This would have the opposite issue of some NPCs reveal species without giving their name. - For species with multiple forms from one region, uncaught forms that have been seen or encountered will still appear in the pokedex after another form has been caught. ## Motivation and Context See linked suggestion. ## How Has This Been Tested? Confirmed both roamer and non-roamer NPC correctly reveals species. Confirmed discovered and seen pokemon display as intended in the pokedex, even when other forms are caught. ## Screenshots (optional): Caught vs seen vs unknown: Celebi revealed by Azalea Town NPC: Roaming Butterfree forms before and after being revealed by Six Island NPC:

The node is fixed by converting to ES6 class.

author: pbarry25
body: Added a GitHub build action for automatically creating a macOS-friendly executable. Similar to the existing build action for creating a Windows executable, this new action uses the same "something was committed to main" trigger and builds on a free-tier macOS runner, creating a `DeepLabCut-Display-macOS` artifact which will run on modern Mac hardware that uses a M1/M2/M3-processor. This new action tested fine in my fork of this repo, and the resulting artifact I was able to download to a M1 MacBookAir and run it fine (example run [here](https://github.com/pbarry25/DeepLabCut-Display/actions/runs/10984945129)).

body:
# Multiple Asset Support (MAS)

## Overview

The Collaborative Bitcoin Custody Solution is a pioneering project in the realm of decentralized finance (DeFi) and digital asset management. Born out of the need for more secure, flexible, and transparent custody solutions in the cryptocurrency space, this project aims to bridge the gap between the decentralized nature of blockchain technologies and the complex requirements of both individual and institutional asset management.

Key objectives of the solution include:

1. Enhancing security through decentralized control and multi-party approvals
2. Providing flexibility to accommodate various organizational structures and use cases
3. Offering granular control over fund management and user permissions
4. Ensuring transparency and auditability of all operations
5. Balancing security with usability for a wide range of users, from individuals to large institutions
6. Adapting to the evolving landscape of digital assets and blockchain technologies

The solution has evolved through several critical phases, each adding crucial functionality:

1. **Multi-signature Wallet Core**: The foundation of our system, allowing multiple parties to control funds collectively. This feature prevents single points of failure and enhances security by requiring multiple approvals for transactions.

2. **Time-locked Transactions**: This feature introduced temporal controls, allowing users to schedule transactions for future execution. It enhances security by providing cool-down periods for large transactions and enables use cases like scheduled payments or vesting schedules.

3. **Individual Spending Limits**: This addition brought granular financial controls, allowing different users to have different transaction limits. It's particularly useful for organizational use cases, enabling hierarchical control structures and risk management.

4. **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)**: This feature introduced sophisticated permission management to our wallet system. RBAC allows for precise control over who can perform specific actions within the wallet, enabling complex organizational structures and enhancing overall security.

5. **Multiple Asset Support** [Current Implementation]: This feature, which is the focus of this pull request, transforms our solution from a Bitcoin-specific wallet into a comprehensive digital asset custody platform. It allows the system to manage a diverse portfolio of cryptocurrencies and tokens, greatly expanding its utility and relevance in the modern crypto ecosystem.

The implementation of multiple asset support represents a significant milestone in this project's roadmap. It addresses several critical needs in the evolving digital asset landscape:

1. **Portfolio Diversification**: As the cryptocurrency space expands beyond Bitcoin, users and organizations need solutions that can manage a variety of assets securely.

2. **Interoperability**: With the rise of cross-chain technologies and multi-chain ecosystems, a custody solution that can handle multiple asset types becomes crucial for seamless operations.

3. **Regulatory Compliance**: Different assets may have varying regulatory requirements. Our system now provides a framework to implement asset-specific compliance measures.

4. **Institutional Adoption**: Many institutions require custody solutions that can handle their diverse digital asset portfolios. This feature positions our solution as a viable option for institutional-grade custody.

5. **Future-Proofing**: As new digital assets emerge, our system can now adapt and incorporate them, ensuring long-term relevance and utility.

In the broader context of blockchain and cryptocurrency adoption, Collaborative Bitcoin Custody Solution with multiple asset support addresses key barriers to entry for both individual and institutional players:

- It provides a unified interface for managing diverse digital assets, simplifying portfolio management.
- It maintains a consistent security model across different asset types, reducing the complexity of securing multiple cryptocurrencies.
- It allows organizations to implement uniform governance policies across various digital assets, streamlining operations and risk management.

Looking forward, the implementation of multiple asset support sets the stage for further enhancements:

1. Integration with decentralized exchanges (DEXs) for in-wallet trading capabilities
2. Cross-chain transaction support for interoperability between different blockchain networks
3. Advanced analytics and reporting features for portfolio performance tracking
4. Integration with external oracles for real-time asset valuation and risk assessment

## Changes Made

### 1. New Trait Definition

Introduced a trait to ensure compatibility with various asset types:

```clarity
(define-trait supported-asset-trait
  (
    (transfer (uint principal principal) (response bool uint))
    (get-balance (principal) (response uint uint))
  )
)
```

This trait defines the minimum interface that any supported asset must implement.

### 2. Updated Supported Assets Map

Modified the `supported-assets` map to track which assets are supported by the wallet:

```clarity
(define-map supported-assets principal bool)
```

### 3. Updated Pending Transactions Map

Updated the `pending-transactions` map to include the asset type for each transaction:

```clarity
(define-map pending-transactions
  uint
  {
    asset: principal,
    amount: uint,
    to: principal,
    approvals: uint,
    executed: bool,
    lock-until: uint,
    submitter: principal
  }
)
```

### 4. Modified Spending Limits Map

Updated the `spending-limits` map to be asset-specific:

```clarity
(define-map spending-limits { owner: principal, asset: principal } uint)
```

### 5. New Function: `add-supported-asset`

Added a new function to allow admins to add new asset types:

```clarity
(define-public (add-supported-asset (asset principal))
  (begin
    (asserts! (is-admin tx-sender) ERR_UNAUTHORIZED)
    (map-set supported-assets asset true)
    (ok true)
  )
)
```

### 6. New Function: `verify-asset`

Added a function to verify that an asset implements the required trait:

```clarity
(define-public (verify-asset (asset principal))
  (begin
    (asserts! (is-admin tx-sender) ERR_UNAUTHORIZED)
    (asserts! (is-some (map-get? supported-assets asset)) ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ASSET)
    (contract-call? asset get-balance CONTRACT_OWNER)
  )
)
```

### 7. Updated `submit-transaction` Function

Modified the `submit-transaction` function to work with multiple asset types:

```clarity

  (let
    (

      (sender-limit (default-to u0 (map-get? spending-limits { owner: tx-sender, asset: asset })))
```
